1.title: Exam Technique and Final Review
1.text: Welcome to Module nineteen: Exam Technique and Final Review. This module covers pacing, method and final review. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. A time plan for sixty-three items in one hundred twenty minutes. A method to read an item, find the binding constraint and eliminate distractors. How to handle multiple-response items. Policies and logistics on exam day. A final review checklist and a plan for the last week.

1.title: Case Check-In: Lumen Advisory
1.text: Our running case is Lumen Advisory. Lumen Advisory. The architect meets the topic of this module. Your job: decide, step by step, which design choice fits best.

1.title: Time Plan
1.text: Time Plan. The figure shows this: Time plan for sixty-three items in one hundred twenty minutes: a first pass of about eighty-five minutes, twenty-five minutes for marked items, ten minutes for final checks. sixty-three items in one hundred twenty minutes is about one minute fifty-four seconds per item; scenario items are longer, so pace yourself. First pass (about eighty-five minutes): answer what you know in about eighty seconds, mark the rest. Second pass (about twenty-five minutes): work the marked items.

1.title: Time Plan, continued
1.text: Time Plan, continued. Last ten minutes: check multiple-response counts and blanks. Never leave an item blank. Do not spend more than about three minutes on one item in the first pass. Only the total scaled score (seven hundred twenty) decides pass or fail. Exam tip: Architect items are scenario-heavy. Read for the constraint and the symptom; the stem usually contains the clue that rules out most options.

1.title: Reading an Item
1.text: Reading an Item. Read the last sentence first ("which change best...", "what is the most likely first place to investigate?") and note how many answers. Find the binding constraint in the stem: latency, cost, security, compliance, accuracy, maintainability, scale. Predict the answer before reading the options. Compare options with the ten decision rules (Module zero) and the chooser (Module eighteen).

1.title: Reading an Item, continued
1.text: Reading an Item, continued. "least privilege", "role only needs". Remove the capability. "same prompt every request", "latency and cost". Cache the stable prefix, static first. "after a document refresh", "confident but wrong". Retrieval and indexing. "exact identifiers", "clause numbers". Keyword or hybrid retrieval. "totals", "aggregations", "table". Structured query, not vector search. "hundreds of tools", "tool selection errors". Tool search or progressive discovery. "steps known in advance". Workflow. "path depends on discoveries", "unpredictable subtasks". Orchestrator-workers or agent. "independent branches, beyond one context". Multi-agent (cost aware). "who is the user", "shared account". Per-user identity and authorization in code.

1.title: Reading an Item, continued
1.text: Reading an Item, continued. "P H I" or "federal" or "E U personal data". B A A and eligible features or Fed R A M P route or D P A, minimization, residency. "before releasing a change". Offline eval, A or B or canary, baseline. "irreversible", "regulated decision". Human approval gate. "client wants a guarantee". Honest, measurable S L A (service level agreement). "team cannot override". Managed settings. Exam tip: The correct option usually removes the cause (least privilege, retrieval fix, caching) instead of adding a detective control or a bigger model.

1.title: Eliminating Distractors
1.text: Eliminating Distractors. Cross out options that. Add logging, confirmation or monitoring where the real fix is removal or prevention. Rely on a stronger prompt or a bigger model for a design or security problem. Use an agent or multi-agent design for a fixed task. Truncate needed context or shrink the model without evidence. Use vector search for exact or aggregate queries. Skip evaluation or judge by anecdote. Use shared credentials, secrets client-side or tokens in U R L s (uniform resource locator). Promise absolutes (one hundred percent accuracy, zero risk). Assume compliance without contract, feature eligibility or route. Exam tip: Change an answer only when you can name the rule it breaks.

1.title: Multiple-response items
1.text: Multiple-response items. Choose exactly the stated number; judge each option on its own merits. Eliminate clearly wrong options first; pairs are often two independent good practices (for example a control and a measure).

1.title: Policies and Logistics
1.text: Policies and Logistics. Registration. Through the Anthropic Partner Academy and Pearson V U E; online proctored or test center. Reschedule or cancel. Up to twenty-four hours before; later changes forfeit the fee. I D. Valid, unexpired government photo I D; the name must match the registration exactly. Accommodations. Request and get approval from Pearson V U E before scheduling. Agreements. You accept a confidentiality and non-disclosure agreement; never share exam content. Conduct. Stay in view of the webcam if online; clear desk; no phones, watches, headphones or notes. Retakes. fourteen or thirty or ninety days; max four attempts per rolling twelve months; fee per attempt.

1.title: Policies and Logistics, continued
1.text: Policies and Logistics, continued. Result. Pass or fail and scaled score, plus percent correct per domain. Validity and renewal. twelve months; on-time renewal is a free, non-proctored assessment; a lapsed credential needs the full exam. Appeals. Within fourteen days through Pearson V U E support; scoring standard and items are not appealable. The guide is version one point zero (July two thousand twenty-six). Check the Partner Academy for the current guide, fee and rules before you book.

1.title: Final Review Checklist
1.text: Final Review Checklist. [ ] I can state the ten decision rules and name the right pattern for a problem shape. [ ] I can justify a model tier with evals and name the levers for cost and latency. [ ] I know caching rules and what breaks them. [ ] I can audit for capability bloat and choose tool search or code execution with M C P (Model Context Protocol). [ ] I can find authorization gaps and explain M C P OAuth (audience, no passthrough, step-up). [ ] I can design a R A G pipeline (chunking, hybrid index, contextual retrieval, rerank, freshness) and say when not to. [ ] I can match retrieval to data shape and explain accuracy-latency trade-offs.

1.title: Final Review Checklist, continued
1.text: Final Review Checklist, continued. [ ] I can define metrics and datasets, grade with mixed methods and run A or B tests. [ ] I can diagnose by layer and optimize cost per successful task. [ ] I can design layered guardrails and human oversight. [ ] I can map G D P R, H I P A A and Fed R A M P to platform and contract choices, and test for bias. [ ] I can run discovery, communicate trade-offs, set honest S L A s, and plan documentation and lifecycle. [ ] I can configure Claude Code for a team with managed settings, Claude dot M D, hooks and telemetry. [ ] I have built one end-to-end solution with R A G, evaluation and observability.

1.title: The last week
1.text: The last week. Seven to four days before: reread the notes of Integration, Solution Design and Evaluation, redo their scenario questions, and write down every miss with the reason. Three days before: walk through the decision chooser (Module eighteen) aloud; reread the names and values table. The day before: light review only: the ten decision rules and the time plan. Check your I D, registration name and test setup, and sleep. On the day: arrive or log in early, read each item's last sentence first, and keep to the time plan.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Time: About one minute fifty-four seconds per item; first pass about eighty-five minutes; mark and return. Method: Last sentence first, binding constraint, predict, eliminate. Pick: Removes the cause, simple, least-privileged, measured, compliant. Multiple response: Choose exactly the stated number. I D: Name must match registration exactly. Cancel: At least twenty-four hours before. Retake: fourteen or thirty or ninety days; max four per rolling twelve months. Pass: seven hundred twenty scaled of one hundred to one thousand; total score only. Valid: twelve months; free on-time renewal assessment. In the next module, we continue the course.
